article.title: Break the ice
article.description: Meaning: to say or do something that relieves tension or awkwardness, especially when meeting people for the first time. Example: 'She told a joke to break the ice at the start of the meeting.' Common mistake: learners sometimes say 'break ice' without 'the'. Origin note: comes from ships literally breaking ice to allow passage.

generated.caption:
Ever felt awkward meeting new people and wished you had the perfect phrase? Learn to "break the ice"!

This idiom means to say or do something that relieves tension or awkwardness, especially when you first meet someone. Remember to always use "the" in this phrase!

Example: "She told a joke to break the ice at the start of the meeting."

Save this tip & follow @englishvault for daily lessons!
generated.script:
Aap bhi kabhi ‘break ice’ bol dete ho kya? Nahin, ye galat hai! Sahi idiom hai ‘break the ice’. Ye dono mein bohot confusion hota hai na?

‘Break the ice’ ka matlab hai jab aap kisi new group ya logon se pehli baar milte ho aur wahan ek awkward silence ya tension ho, toh usko khatam karne ke liye kuch bolna ya karna. Basically, mahaul ko thoda comfortable banana. Jaise ki, 'She told a joke to break the ice at the start of the meeting.' Matlab usne meeting shuru hone se pehle ek joke sunaya taaki sab comfortable ho jayein.

Toh ab se jab bhi kisi new situation mein tension ya awkwardness ko relieve karna ho, toh hamesha 'break the ice' use karna. Never just 'break ice'. Ab samajh aaya?

Comment mein batao aapko ye pehle se pata tha ya nahin! Aur aise hi English tips ke liye The English Vault ko follow karo!

slides.body: To 'break the ice' means to say or do something that helps relieve tension or awkwardness, especially when people are meeting for the first time. For instance, she told a joke to break the ice at the start of the meeting. A common mistake learners make is to omit 'the' — remember, it's always 'break *the* ice', never just 'break ice'.
